sections.h2: Less than half of India's LPG travels by pipeline

chart.title: Pipeline share of LPG ranges from 34% in the north to 49% in the south
chart.sub: Share of LPG moved by pipeline by region, %; national figure 45%.

sections.means: The committee's own tally puts LPG pipeline share at 45% nationally, with the North-East having no LPG pipelines at all.
sections.todo: Connect nearby bottling plants to existing common-carrier pipelines rather than trucking to them, as the committee recommends.

sections.h2: Petroleum products depend on rail, with road close to negligible

chart.title: Rail carries about 29% of petroleum products, and road only about 1%
chart.sub: Share of petroleum products moved by each mode nationally, %.

sections.means: Pipelines carry most petroleum products, and the committee says rail remains essential because pipelines cannot replace it entirely.
sections.todo: Keep rail capacity in the plan, and add rail-unloading facilities where they cut specific road movement, as the committee proposes.

sections.h2: Pipeline utilisation ranges from 7.9% to 165.3% of declared capacity

chart.title: Several FY26 pipelines run above their declared capacity, the highest at 165.3%
chart.sub: Utilisation, FY26, % of declared capacity, highest first.
chart.source: PNGRB Expert Committee report, July 2026 (pipeline register).

sections.means: The committee's register shows wide spread between pipelines, from Panipat–Delhi at 7.9% to Haldia–Mourigram–Rajbandh at 165.3%.
sections.todo: Read utilisation figures against each line's history, since over-100% lines may be debottlenecked and low-use lines may be newly built for future demand.
